78,590 dated events across 504 companies · 1994-06-03 to 2026-08-28 · forward book: 193 announced, 99 projected

What is in here

Every dated corporate action the platform holds, unified from twelve separate sources: results and board meetings, dividends and splits and buybacks, AGM voting outcomes, credit-rating actions, auditor and key-person changes, orders and acquisitions and capex, regulatory and US-FDA actions, bulk and block prints, promoter and insider trades, and ticker changes. Each row keeps the source it came from and links back to it.

Identity

Coming up

The forward book. Announced dates are ones the company itself has filed — a board meeting called for results, an ex-date already fixed. Estimated dates are projected from that company's own filing history and are marked as such, with the range of the history behind them; no company has announced them and they should not be relied on as if it had.

ANNOUNCED — filed by the company ~ ESTIMATED — projected from filing history, not announced

Already happened — last 12 months, material only

High-materiality events only: rating upgrades and downgrades, auditor resignations, CEO and CFO exits, acquisitions and order wins, regulatory and FDA actions, promoter trades, splits and buybacks, and every results date. Routine filings — 13,282 board appointments, reaffirmed ratings, uncontested resolutions — are held in the table but kept off this view, because listing them here would bury the handful that changed something. Search or filter to reach anything.

Method

Built by features/80_event_calendar.py from tables the platform already maintains — nothing here is scraped separately, so the calendar is exactly as current as its sources. Events are aggregated to what a reader would call one event: 130,537 voting resolutions are 9,430 meetings, and a downgrade across eight instruments on one morning is one downgrade. Where two sources describe the same event differently — NSE records a dividend as declared, Yahoo restates it for later splits — the exchange's own record wins and keeps its provenance. Estimated results dates use the median gap between quarter-end and board meeting over that company's last eight filings, and are only produced where there are at least four to measure.
